claims.statement: Paraphe requires only Python 3.11 or newer and no third-party dependency at runtime; the install fetches the build backend once.
A local run needs exactly two operator-supplied values: a create bearer for the agent and a different answer credential for the owner.
Adding a bot token and the owner Telegram id switches the destination to the phone, and the answer credential becomes optional because the owner answers by tapping.
The local route reaches a ready server, refuses the agent credential on the answer path, accepts the owner answer, resumes the agent by polling, and closes the card, with no external service.

The container image keeps its data outside the image on a mounted volume and runs as the unprivileged paraphe user, so the mounted directory has to be writable by that user; it keeps the default loopback bind inside the container, so publishing the port is not a route to an answerable inbox.
The store defaults to the operator's per-user data directory and can be pointed elsewhere with the store_path configuration key.

The in-repository contracts remain docs/tools.md for the tool surface and docs/adapters.md for destinations — the recorded demo cites both — even though neither appears in the README's documentation table any more.

The shell client completes the loop without tool bindings: paraphe ask creates the card over the MCP surface and prints the request id on stdout, and a backgrounded paraphe wait <request_id> holds the card's lifetime in repeated bounded windows, exiting 0 answered, 3 expired or not answerable, and 4 unknown request id.

The default bind is loopback 127.0.0.1:8787 for both the server (runtime.DEFAULT_MCP_PORT) and the shell client (cli.DEFAULT_PORT), and the ready line is printed from the socket that was actually bound with the port it reports, so a run that sets PARAPHE_MCP_PORT — as the recorded demo did with 8899 — prints that port instead of the default.

The create bearer an agent holds creates and reads cards but cannot answer one, a local run is refused at setup without an owner answer credential, and setup refuses an answer credential equal to the create bearer.

When no store_path is configured, resolving the default store location while a store exists only at the legacy /var/lib/paraphe/inbox.sqlite raises a setup error naming both paths rather than starting a second, empty inbox.

The owner answers a card through one of three channels — a tap on the Telegram keyboard, a long-press reply to the card message, or the owner-only local answer path — and the card records which one actually delivered the answer in `responded_via` (`telegram`, `telegram-reply`, `answer-path`).

The Telegram destination renders a decision card with `render_card` in a fixed section order (identity line, kind line, bold title, context, numbered options, Recommended, If approved, Limits, links, reply hint, expiry) with every interpolated value escaped and oversized free text trimmed deterministically under a message budget, whereas a status (`notify`) message renders only the identity line, title and message and carries no keyboard.

Every decision card ends with the reply hint telling the owner that replying to the message answers it in their own words or asks a question, while a reply to a status message is not a card message and records nothing.

The console destination composes its own plain-text layout from the same notification payload — including the `curl` command that answers the card through the owner answer path — rather than reusing the phone card renderer, so layout belongs to each destination.

The answer returns through the ask itself by any of three equal routes — a call parked with `wait_seconds`, a backgrounded `paraphe wait` holding the card's whole lifetime, or a boundary drain with `get_response` / `list_unprocessed` at the next run — so no chat message and no server-initiated turn is required.

Alongside the wiki pages, the quickstart points readers at the repository references that own the adjacent contracts: `docs/tools.md` (tool surface), `docs/adapters.md` (destinations), `skills/paraphe-return-path/SKILL.md` (async return protocol), `CONTEXT.md` (vocabulary), `docs/adr/` (decisions), `docs/specs/paraphe-v1.md` (v1 specification) and `docs/roadmap.md`.

Reaching the process from outside means the phone destination with the answer credential unset and a loopback or Tailnet bind: Runtime.start raises SetupError for a non-loopback host whenever an answer credential is configured, and serve_inbox raises BindError for any host that is not loopback or in a Tailnet range, so the README's PARAPHE_MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0 recipe is refused as a public wildcard rather than served.

config.example.toml ships bot_token and owner_telegram_id placeholder lines, and a non-empty bot token is what selects the phone destination, so a copy of that file left unchanged is a phone run: a local console run must delete those two lines, and a phone run requires a positive owner Telegram id.
paraphe.toml is git-ignored, so the credential file the operator fills in is not committed by default.

Showing the card is best effort and the durable store is the source of the answer, so a notification or wake that never arrived is not a lost decision and a run that missed the parked call and the shell wait drains the answer later.
The owner's long-press reply may be a question rather than a decision: a reply that is a question or not a decision is not executed, and the agent explains and re-asks with a fresh card.

AGENTS.md is the repository's canonical instruction file, and its Card surface section summarizes the Telegram card's ordered sections and the owner's long-press reply entering the same claim path as a tap, with the detail owned by the card rendering and reply pages.

AGENTS.md's OpenWiki note records that the generated openwiki/ index is optional just-in-time context refreshed by a scheduled workflow rather than required startup reading, with source code and tests staying authoritative.

Besides paraphe.toml, the repository's .gitignore marks the local-only run artifacts as never tracked — docs/plans/*.companion.md, docs/plans/*.goal.txt and the in-flight openwiki/.run.json — so a working checkout commits none of them, and the OpenWiki update workflow deletes the transient .run.json after each run.

The README's documentation table now points at the generated wiki — openwiki/index.md, openwiki/quickstart.md and openwiki/architecture/ — so docs/tools.md and docs/adapters.md were dropped from it while the other in-repo documents (CONTEXT.md, docs/adr/, docs/specs/paraphe-v1.md, docs/roadmap.md, skills/paraphe-return-path/SKILL.md) remain listed.

The phone route starts by proving the configured destination with `paraphe check telegram` before starting the server: the check names the bot and sends one plain setup message to the owner, prints no token, and creates no decision card.

The documented upgrade path for a store left at the legacy /var/lib/paraphe/inbox.sqlite is `paraphe store relocate`, which copies it to the current per-user default, verifies the SQLite copy before installing it and keeps the old store as a backup; `paraphe store relocate --move` removes the source instead, and setting store_path to the old location remains available when relocation is not wanted.

The installed `paraphe` command's working forms are the server start with an optional `--config PATH`, `ask QUESTION`, `wait REQUEST_ID`, `check telegram`, `store relocate [--move]`, and `--version`/`--help`, which is what the entry point's usage text documents.
